Clinical details:
Late-presenting anterior STEMI 2023. Three-vessel coronary disease at angiography. LVEF approximately 30% on echo. Viability assessment prior to consideration of CABG.

Technique:
Cardiac MRI at 1.5 T (viability protocol). Cine SSFP imaging in standard long- and short-axis planes and late gadolinium enhancement imaging following 0.1 mmol/kg gadobutrol. T2-weighted imaging and parametric mapping were not acquired.

Findings:
The left ventricle is mildly dilated with thinning of the apical and mid anterior walls (end-diastolic thickness 4 mm) and severely impaired systolic function. The apex and apical segments are akinetic with a small apical aneurysm; the mid anterior and anteroseptal segments are severely hypokinetic. LVEDVi 118 ml/m², LVESVi 81 ml/m², LVEF 31%, LV mass index 66 g/m².

The right ventricle is normal in size with preserved systolic function. RVEDVi 78 ml/m², RVESVi 35 ml/m², RVEF 55%.

The atria are not dilated. No significant valvular regurgitation or stenosis.

No pericardial effusion. No significant extracardiac findings.

Late gadolinium enhancement:
Subendocardial enhancement in the LAD territory: transmural (>75%) in the apex and all apical segments, 51–75% in the mid anterior and mid anteroseptal segments, and 1–25% in the basal anterior segment. No enhancement of the inferior or lateral walls. Segments with less than 50% transmural extent are likely to be viable; those with greater than 50% are unlikely to recover function following revascularisation. No apical thrombus on early or late post-contrast imaging.

Conclusion:
1. Chronic LAD territory infarction with severely impaired left ventricular systolic function (LVEF 31%) and a small apical aneurysm.
2. Non-viable apex and apical segments. The mid anterior and mid anteroseptal segments (51–75% transmural extent) are unlikely to recover function.
3. Viable myocardium in the basal anterior segment and throughout the RCA and circumflex territories.
4. Suggest discussion at the heart team MDT.
